en: Text for Casting Sand Buddhas:
I reverently address the Pure Dharma Body within the Lotus Treasury World; the ten billion Tathāgatas and the transformation Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
the Great Sage Mañjuśrī atop Mount Qingliang; and the Arhats who attained the Way at Mount Kukkuṭapāda.
The secret scriptures of the Dragon Palace and the subtle words of Vulture Peak;
may all the worthy and holy ones, with their divine eyes and knowledge of others' minds,
deign to manifest their supernormal powers.
Moving with compassion,
descend upon this ritual site to bear witness to our meritorious virtues.
Nowadays, pure altars have been established throughout the eight directions,
and Buddha images are displayed at the four gates;
in the center is erected the sanctuary of Avalokiteśvara.
The Section on the Assembly of Śākyas Turning the Golden Words:
To establish offerings of incense and fine food for the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
and to scatter pure food upon the sentient beings of both water and land.
That the entire realm offers reverent devotion and the whole city bows its heads in earnest supplication—who is it for whom this is performed?

It is precisely because of the Great Protector of our court, whose auspicious blessings have gathered to dispel calamities. We humbly reflect that the lineage and ancestral records of our Great Protector have been passed down through generations.
He should be worthy of the five hundred sages;
endowed with the pure birth of a mountain or river,
he shall surely be among the thousand worthies of the latter age.
His literary excellence surpassed that of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius;
his calligraphy entered the wood with its characteristic sevenfold strokes.
Bending his bow, he pierced the floating target as he released the arrow.
Monkeys wailed as they circled the tree; Kuan-hung governed the multitude with broad magnanimity.
The myriad people sighed in wonder at the auspicious wind of his virtue;
he established the Dharma to bring peace to the people.
A thousand households celebrate the auspiciousness of a new year;
furthermore, with faith as a bright pearl, the mirror of the mind is first made clear.
Relying upon the teachings of Śākyamuni, the eight directions are brought to order.
I revere the sages and worthies to bring peace to the state;
first, I set forth my sincere aspirations.
Facing Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, I incline my heart toward it.
He invited the Buddha and the Sangha,
established a pure altar on the Ninth Ground,
and recited the sutras throughout the six periods of the day; the sound of the chanting resonated through the entire city until dawn.
The officials and commoners entreated Heaven;
the bells and Buddhist chants resounded loudly throughout the city.
At that time, the sun shone from the north.
The frozen ice melted and harmonized with the surroundings.
As the monks completed their recitations, the sincerity of the consecration ceremony reached its full measure after five days; all these manifold merits were thus accumulated.
First, may the infinite causes of adornment be employed:
Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the eight classes of dragon deities.
We pray that their majestic radiance may further increase.
The power of merit increases ever further, promoting fortune and compassion;
saving sentient beings and protecting the nation,
may the current sagely sovereign sit forever upon the imperial throne.
Ten paths race toward one goal as their red hearts turn toward the state;
moreover, this is specifically for the merit that serves as adornment for my Grand Protector’s noble station.
I humbly pray that your blessings may be as vast as the oceans and mountains,
forever maintaining your steadfast integrity and welcoming auspiciousness;
and that your emolument may reach the limits of the Yangtze and Huai Rivers.
Having governed Hexi and succeeded to the throne,
the state enjoys great auspiciousness that increases like the sun and moon until they become full.
The Princess and her Consort shall enjoy eternal prosperity, preserving their fragrant countenances forever pure.
May the Cishi, Shangshu, and others firmly accept this vow to follow one after another in succession to propagate and flourish [the Dharma].
May all the young ladies welcome longevity with pure and radiant virtue.
Only then shall the rivers clear and the seas be calm, and the sounds of sorrow and suffering no longer be heard.
The four [kings] gradually descend to bring peace, forever severing the warfare of smoke and dust;
the three calamities are utterly extinguished, and the nine untimely deaths are eliminated throughout the seas and borders.
Pestilence is suppressed and disasters are dispelled.
It sends relief from famine to the realms of the earth,
dispersing its moisture throughout the entire Dharma-realm and reaching all classes of sentient beings.
In this city of the Supreme Cause, one ascends the path to enlightenment through the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
Indeed, during vast and noble great kalpas, there have been sages;
one such as emerged from the palace of the Śākya clan was named Bhagavān.
The mind is concentrated in great stillness, while body and thought are boundless;
through compassionate transformation of sentient beings, one is titled a Buddha.
This is because he now sits before us with feet level and even.
On the fourth day of the first month of the third spring,
those who have offered prayers for the initial restoration of the stupa’s seal and its sand [filling] have convened this assembly of merit and blessings to personally ensure their preservation.
Only you, sir, have long manifested a voice like golden bells and early on acquired a reputation as pure as jade.
Having ascended to a distinguished rank and attained the honorable office of a high official,
you have thus wondrously turned back the seeds planted in past lives, causing their sprouts of goodness to blossom in this present life.
With the fruits of karma already purified and the mind of the Way firmly established,
on this day the four elements ceased their flow at dawn,
and the five aggregates were all empty and liberated.
The true countenance of the Thousand Li [Buddha] seals the pervasive traces as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
furthermore, one may burn incense,
emulating the various monastic disciples of the outside world prior to meritorious rites.
Distribute the food throughout all places, both on land and in water. With this seal,
dedicate the merit of the Buddha’s virtues as a cause for blessings,
first adorning the Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, the Nāgas, and the eight classes of devas.
I humbly pray that your majestic radiance may grow ever more sublime and your power of merit ever more augmented, so as to save sentient beings and protect the state.
May Your Holiness enjoy a long life, the five grains flourish,
the people within your jurisdiction live in peace, and songs of joy fill the city.
Furthermore, may the donor’s very person be adorned by the mastery of supreme merit;
may their body be like a jade tree, eternally pure and eternally radiant,
and like a vajra, forever firm and ever-solid.
In this life and in future lives, may no wholesome conditions be severed.
May the sprouts of virtue grow in this world and in other births,
thereafter spreading throughout the entire realm of phenomena and reaching all classes of sentient beings.
This supreme cause, which brings one equally to the fruition of Buddhahood, is the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
